title: Checkmate Patterns
description: Learn the classic ways to checkmate: the back rank, rook and queen mates, the smothered mate, and the quick traps called Scholar's mate and Fool's mate. You will also learn how to defend.

chapters.title: Mating with rooks and the queen
Quick mates and how to stop them

moves.comment: The rook checks the king. The pawns block f7, g7 and h7. The rook also covers f8 and h8. No escape, so it is checkmate.

steps.intro: The black king is stuck behind its own pawns. A rook check on the back row can be checkmate.

moves.comment: The same idea. The pawns trap their own king.

hints: Go to the eighth row, on the d-file.
steps.intro: White to move. Find the checkmate.
Look at the position after the checkmate.
steps.question: Why can the black king not escape after Rd8?
choices: Its own pawns block the squares in front of it
The king is not allowed to move sideways
steps.explanation: The pawns on f7, g7 and h7 take away the squares in front of the king, and the rook covers the squares beside it.

points: The back rank is the row where the king starts
The king's own pawns can trap it
A rook or queen on an open file does the job
mistakes: Moving all the pawns in front of the king without making an escape square
Forgetting to check whether the file is open
questions: Which black pieces are blocking the king's escape?
Which squares does the rook attack on the eighth rank?

moves.comment: A small pawn move. Now the h7 square is empty.
Check, but this time the king has a way out.
The king steps to h7. No checkmate!

steps.intro: It is Black's move. White threatens Re8 checkmate. Black needs an escape square.

moves.comment: Now the king can use h7.

hints: Move the h-pawn one step, to h6.
steps.intro: Black to move. Push the h-pawn one square to make a window for the king.

steps.question: Black to move. Which idea stops the checkmate?
choices: Move a pawn to give the king an escape square
steps.explanation: A pawn move such as h6 gives the king a square. Kh8 still loses to Re8 checkmate.

points: Luft is a German word for air. It means an escape square for the king
Kids should check their own back rank every few moves
Any one of the f, g or h pawns can make the window
mistakes: Waiting until the rook is already on the file
Pushing a pawn that does not open a square next to the king
questions: Which squares could the king use after one pawn moves?
When should you make the window, now or later?

moves.comment: White offers a trade.
The black rook has to capture or the king is lost.
The second rook takes back. It is checkmate again.

steps.intro: Black has a rook guarding the back row. White has two rooks on the e-file.

moves.comment: Checkmate.

hints: Check on e8 with the rook on e2.
steps.intro: White to move. Find the line. Start with the check on e8.

hints: Offer a trade on the e8 square.
steps.intro: Play the whole line as White.

points: Two rooks together are stronger than one guard
Each trade keeps the attacker in charge
Count attackers and defenders of the e8 square
mistakes: Checking with only one rook when Black can take it for free
Forgetting that the black rook can take back
questions: How many white pieces attack e8?
How many black pieces guard it?

chapterList.title: Mating with rooks and the queen

lessons.title: The ladder mate with two rooks

moves.comment: The rook on b7 covers the whole seventh row. The king may only move along the back row.
The rook on a8 checks along the back row. The rook on b7 guards the row below. Checkmate.

steps.intro: Two rooks can be a ladder. One rook cuts off a whole row. Then the other rook gives check on the edge.

moves.comment: The king cannot go down or to the side.

hints: Use the rook that is not on the seventh row.
steps.intro: White to move. The rook on b7 already blocks the seventh row. Find the checkmate.

points: Two rooks take turns building a wall that pushes the king to the edge
One rook cuts off a row and the other gives check
Keep the rooks far apart on the board so the king cannot attack them
mistakes: Putting the two rooks next to each other where the king can attack them
Giving a check that lets the king run back
questions: Why does the rook on b7 matter?
Which rows can the king not use now?

moves.comment: The queen checks the king. The white king guards the queen, so the black king cannot take it. Every other square is covered.

steps.intro: White's king is close to the black king. The queen can come in and be guarded.

moves.comment: The queen is guarded by the king. The black king has no safe square.

hints: Go to the b7 square. Your king guards it.
steps.intro: White to move. Find the checkmate in the corner.

points: A lone king can be mated by the king and queen working together
The queen gives check while the king guards the queen
A queen next to the enemy king is only safe when it is guarded (here, by your king)
mistakes: Putting the queen next to the king without a guard, so the king captures it
Checking from far away when a closer check is mate
questions: Which white piece guards the queen on g7?
Why can the black king not take the queen?

moves.comment: Oops! The king is not in check, and every square it could use is covered. Black has no legal move.

steps.intro: White is winning easily. But one wrong queen move gives a draw.

moves.comment: Checkmate, not stalemate. The king is in check.

hints: Go to g7, right next to the king, guarded by your own king.
steps.intro: Same position. White to move. Find the checkmate instead of the stalemate.
Look at the position after the queen move.
steps.question: After Qg6 it is Black's turn. The king is not in check and has no legal move. What is this?
steps.explanation: The king is not attacked, but it cannot move anywhere safe and Black has no other piece. That is stalemate, and the game is a draw.

points: Stalemate means the player to move has no legal move and is not in check
It is a draw, not a win
Before a quiet move, always ask what squares the enemy king has left
mistakes: Taking away every square from the enemy king without giving check
Playing fast when you are winning
questions: What is the difference between checkmate and stalemate?
What should you count before every move when you are far ahead?

moves.comment: The knight jumps to f7 and checks the king on h8. Nothing can take the knight and the king cannot move. This is a smothered mate.

steps.intro: The black king sits in the corner. Its own rook and pawns box it in.

moves.comment: Smothered mate again.

steps.intro: White to move. This is the same pattern on the other side. Find the checkmate.
Look at the position before the knight move.
steps.question: Why is a knight the best piece to give a smothered mate?
choices: It jumps, so nothing can block its check
steps.explanation: A knight jumps over pieces. The king cannot hide behind anything.

points: Smothered means the king is blocked by its own pieces
A knight is perfect for this check, because it jumps and cannot be blocked
The corner is where it happens most
mistakes: Trying it with a bishop or rook, which can be blocked or taken
Forgetting to check that no black piece can take the knight
questions: Which black pieces smother the king?
Why can a knight check a king that is fully surrounded?

lessons.title: A smothered mate in the opening

moves.comment: A tricky move. The knight attacks the knight on f3.
White grabs a pawn. Not a mistake yet, but White must be careful now.
The queen attacks the knight on e5 and the pawn on g2.
Too greedy! This is the real mistake.
Black takes g2 and attacks the rook on h1 too.
Check.
Another mistake. 7.Qe2 would avoid the mate.
A smothered mate. The king is boxed in by its own pieces. The bishop on e2 cannot take the knight, because the queen on e4 pins it to the king.

steps.intro: Black tries an early trap. Watch what happens if White grabs pawns.

moves.comment: Checkmate. Every square near the king is taken by White's own pieces or covered.

steps.intro: Black to move. The white king is boxed in. Find the checkmate.

hints: Black plays a knight to d4 on move three.
steps.intro: Play the trap as Black. If White grabs pawns, you win.

points: This trap starts when Black plays 3...Nd4 in the Italian Game
White must not be greedy
The trap works because the white king is stuck behind its own pieces
4.Nxd4 is a simple safe answer
mistakes: Grabbing pawns when the opponent's queen can come out with threats
Blocking a check with a piece that leaves the king boxed in
questions: Which white pieces box in their own king at the end?
Which White move was the real mistake?

chapterList.title: Quick mates and how to stop them

moves.comment: The f-pawn leaves the diagonal open.
Now the g-pawn can never block on g3.
The queen checks along the diagonal. No piece can block it or take the queen, and the king cannot move.

steps.intro: This is the quickest checkmate in chess. It only works if White plays two very weak pawn moves.

moves.comment: Fool's mate.

steps.intro: Black to move. White has played two weak pawn moves. Find the checkmate.
Play the Fool's mate as Black. White helps you by playing badly.

steps.question: Why does Fool's mate work against the white king?
choices: The f-pawn opened the diagonal, and the g-pawn moved past g3, so nothing can block the check
steps.explanation: The f-pawn opened the diagonal, and the g-pawn moved past g3, so nothing can block the check from the queen on h4.

points: This is the fastest possible checkmate, in two moves
It only happens if White helps by moving the f-pawn and the g-pawn
It shows why the e1 to h4 diagonal needs care
mistakes: Moving the f-pawn and g-pawn early without a reason
Not looking at the diagonal that leads to your king
questions: Which two white pawn moves open the diagonal?
Why can no white piece block the check?

moves.comment: The queen comes out.
The bishop joins in. Both pieces attack f7.
This move does not guard f7, so the threat is still there.
The queen takes f7. The bishop guards her, so the king cannot take. Checkmate.

steps.intro: Scholar's mate is a four-move trick. White aims the queen and the bishop at the f7 pawn.

moves.comment: Checkmate.

steps.intro: White to move. Find the checkmate.

hints: Bring the queen out on move two.
steps.intro: Play Scholar's mate as White.

points: The queen and bishop both aim at f7
At the start f7 is guarded only by the king
It works against beginners, but strong players stop it easily
Do not bring the queen out early just to try it
mistakes: Defending with a move that does not guard f7
Playing the trap again and again against players who know the defense
questions: Which two white pieces attack f7?
Which black pieces can guard f7?

moves.comment: The pawn attacks the queen.
The queen moves away but attacks f7 again. Qxf7 checkmate is threatened once more!
The knight steps onto the f-file and blocks the queen, so she cannot reach f7. Black is fine, but keep watching f7. White may try Qb3 next.

steps.intro: Black can stop the trick. The pawn on g6 attacks the queen.

moves.comment: Now the queen must move.

hints: Push the g-pawn one step, to g6.
steps.intro: Black to move. White threatens Qxf7 checkmate. Push the one pawn that attacks the queen and stops the checkmate.

steps.question: Black to move. Which of these moves guards f7 and stops the checkmate?
steps.explanation: The queen on e7 guards f7. Nf6 does not guard f7, and Qxf7 is checkmate.

hints: Attack the queen with a pawn on move three.
steps.intro: Play the defense as Black.

points: Black can attack the queen with a pawn so she must move
Black can also guard f7 with the queen on e7
Never ignore a threat to f7
After the defense, develop pieces calmly
mistakes: Moving the knight to f6 and forgetting f7 is attacked twice
Panicking and pushing random pawns
questions: Which black move attacks the queen?
Why does the queen have to leave h5?
